paper.title: You Only Look at Screens: Multimodal Chain-of-Action Agents
paper.central_claim: Auto-GUI is a multimodal autonomous GUI agent operating without environment parsing or application-dependent APIs; chain-of-action history and predicted future plans yield superior action success/generalization and sub-second action inference.

signatures.object: Screen/instruction/history-to-action policy, replacing an externally parsed textual screen pipeline
signatures.information: Current screenshot, user instruction, past action tuples; frozen BLIP-2 visual features; no DOM/API input in default model. Future action labels are training targets only.
signatures.operation: Project vision to language dimension; language-query/vision-key-value single-head attention and gated fusion; supervised encoder-decoder emits future action types then current action fields.
signatures.output: Action Plan plus Action Decision: action_type, touch_point, lift_point, typed_text
signatures.conditions: AITW training; FLAN-Alpaca initialization; history up to eight and future-plan length four chosen on General analysis. No oracle future frame supplied at inference.
signatures.feedback: Static demonstrated action supervision, not online task-result feedback
signatures.selection_rule/data: Fixed AITW episode-wise 80/10/10 split; supervised training up to ten epochs; no autonomous acceptance/rejection of policy improvements
signatures.persistence: Offline trained parameters; episode action history only. No experience-selected persistent updates.
signatures.later_use: Same fixed model on held-out screenshot steps; runtime prediction is generated, not teacher-provided future actions.
signatures.claimed_effect: Improved action matching and faster inference without screen parsing
signatures.failure_boundary: Wrong clicks/scroll direction and episode drift are not resolved by action-type accuracy; no deployed recovery/verifier measured.

signatures.information: Demonstrated touch/lift coordinates and derived direction during preprocessing
signatures.operation: Round clicks to four decimals and canonicalize scrolling to fixed direction endpoints in relative [y,x] coordinates.
signatures.output: Reduced-ambiguity textual action schema with six action types
signatures.conditions: Assumes fine-grained scroll magnitude/path is dispensable for benchmark actions; click matcher uses tolerance.
signatures.selection_rule/data: Deterministic transformation, not policy improvement selection
signatures.persistence: Static target convention in training and decoder output
signatures.later_use: Applied for held-out action prediction; no cross-platform schema transfer evaluated
signatures.claimed_effect: 4.04-point matching gain relative to no normalization
signatures.failure_boundary: Canonicalization may discard execution-relevant magnitude and does not itself verify task completion.

gap.author_gap: External screen parsing/application-dependent tools and myopic action decisions burden GUI automation; multimodal chain-of-action is proposed as a direct efficient agent.
gap.checked_gap: A concrete screen-to-action interface/context bottleneck exists, but the fixed results identify offline prediction improvements, not closed-loop task success or universal parser removal.

gap.residue: Need efficient screenshot policy with contextual planning that actually succeeds under unseen instructions/apps and accumulated errors.
gap.stakes: Per-step matching can mask incorrect clicks and compounding failures in real user workflows.
gap.method_response: Align visual features to language representations and jointly decode plan/action; canonical gesture targets simplify output learning.
gap.remaining_gap: No online rollout outcomes, no clean instruction/app holdout, no bridge-isolating control; plan/history marginal effects are internally inconsistent.

claims.text: Auto-GUI is a multimodal autonomous GUI agent operating without environment parsing or application-dependent APIs; chain-of-action history and predicted future plans yield superior action success/generalization and sub-second action inference.
claims.setting: AITW static screenshot/action matching, five subsets
claims.baseline/control: BC-history 73.1 average; different pretrained/fine-tuning baselines and information interfaces
claims.selection_vs_test: Episode-wise 80/10/10; unified uses 10% GoogleApps training; history/plan hyperparameter analysis on General, independent model-selection partition details not fully reconstructible
claims.result/denominator: Unified mean 74.27 across five subset scores vs BC-history 73.1; not 74.27% completed episodes; total test-action count not independently tabulated by us
counterevidence: One dataset only (E019), loose coordinate tolerance (E007), richer structured information still helps (E020).
claims.allowed_conclusion: Strong offline action matching of parser-free model on the reported split; no demonstrated online task-completion or transfer rate.

claims.text: Action history and future plan improve action decisions
claims.baseline/control: Full 74.27; joint chain removal 68.53; individual history/plan removals
claims.selection_vs_test: Same reported benchmark split; no multiple-training-seed uncertainty
claims.result/denominator: Joint chain delta +5.74; future/history labels exchange 73.78 and 68.81 between Table 3 and Table 9
counterevidence: Internal label contradiction blocks component-specific marginal interpretation.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Joint chain removal is associated with lower matching; which individual component accounts for which delta remains unresolved.

claims.text: Normalization improves performance and action inference is sub-second
claims.setting: AITW normalized action prediction; eight V100 training setup
claims.baseline/control: No-normalization 70.23; Llama2 speed comparator has different model/data/interface
claims.selection_vs_test: Reported fixed system timing, not live full-task trials
claims.result/denominator: Normalization +4.04 matching points; large feature extraction 0.06s, inference 0.59s, 8.2GB; large training 75h
counterevidence: No browser/device/network/recovery end-to-end latency; omitted unsuccessful rollout costs are not measured.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Sub-second reported model action prediction, not a sub-second completed task or equal-quality system-level cost claim.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported parser-free screenshot/history-to-action prediction attains 74.27 mean AITW matching with sub-second model inference. Joint chain/normalization ablations support aggregate offline effects, not isolated history-versus-plan effect or closed-loop completion.
unresolved: History/plan label swap in Tables 3 and 9.
Unobserved image-only baseline prompt contents and cross-subset heatmap values.
Independent instruction/app generalization and rollout completion not established.
assessment.retention: not_applicable: fixed supervised policy and episodic action context, no persistent selection-and-retention improvement loop
assessment.reproduction: None; no source code executed. All experimental results are author_report.

G.reason: Specific parser/interface and context bottlenecks with BC-history lineage; offline/online distinction exposes real residue, but nearest-neighbor priority and independent-generalization boundary are incompletely tested.

M.reason: Projection, gated fusion, joint future-type/action output and canonical gestures target the bottleneck concretely. The argument that simplified targets/plan generation improve executed behavior remains weaker than the reconstructible operation.

X.reason: Static training/deployment and action fields can be reconstructed; future labels are not privileged inference inputs. No validated recovery/termination loop and image-only baseline prompts remain unknown; card match does not supply these.

E.measurement.reason: A clearly specified, useful offline matcher and prior correlation citation exist, but the original autonomous-system claim is not tested by this policy’s outcome-checked execution. 14%/bounding-box clicks and axis scroll matching are lenient.

E.causality.reason: Consistent joint-chain and normalization removals offer evidence, but individual plan/history labels conflict. Different backbone/data/interface baselines and no bridge-specific control leave major alternative explanations.

E.holdout.reason: Episode holdout and five subsets supply limited in-distribution testing; repeated instructions/apps are not excluded, one dataset only, and cross-subset figures do not establish online transfer.

E.statistics.reason: Subset/category/ablation reporting provides some failure boundaries, but full text §§4–5 and Appendices A–C give no repeated-training uncertainty or CIs; table-label contradiction further limits small differences.

E.cost.reason: Training hardware/hours and per-action feature/inference time/memory are explicit. Timing is not end-to-end and Llama2 comparison lacks matched data/model/quality.

reason: Concrete efficient multimodal action policy with reported offline improvement, but the original autonomous/generalization claim exceeds evidence; history/plan ablation labels conflict and attribution/holdout/online validation remain limited.
